answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to earn a costly, verifiable reputation pearl before it can trade: completing real, jury-graded work that is recorded on a shared ledger. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge — one identity, one history, no shortcuts — so spinning up a thousand hollow copies gains nothing, because none of them carry the earned record. An attacker must pay the full work cost for every fake identity, making a sybil flood expensive while honest agents keep their standing.
